summary.en: To say **why** we do something use **to / in order to / so as to** + infinitive, **so that** + clause, or **for** + noun or -ing. To set a **condition** use **unless** (= if not), **as long as / provided that** (= only if) and **in case** (= because something might happen). Only **in case** looks at a possible problem; the others state a condition.
summary.es: «Para» tiene tres formas: to + infinitivo, so that + oración y for + nombre/-ing. Y «por si acaso» es in case, no if.

form: **to / in order to / so as to** + infinitive (negative: _in order not to_, _so as not to_)
**so that** + subject + can / will / would (_so that we can leave early_)
**for** + noun or -ing: _a knife for cutting bread_
**in case** + present simple (future meaning) or past simple (past meaning)
**unless / as long as / provided (that) / providing** + present simple, with a future or modal in the main clause

uses.text: **Purpose, same subject**: _I'm saving money **to** buy a car._ _She left early **so as not to** miss the train._
**Purpose, different subjects**: _I'll send the files **so that** you can read them tonight._
**In case** = as a precaution: _Take an umbrella **in case** it rains._

note.en: In case is not the same as if: if it rains, I take it; in case it rains, I take it before.
note.es: In case = por si acaso. Se hace antes de que ocurra algo.

uses.text: **Unless** means if not: _We'll cancel the picnic **unless** the weather improves._
**As long as / provided that** = only if: _You can borrow my car **as long as** you drive carefully._

mistakes.wrong: I went to the bank for to pay the bill.
mistakes.right: I went to the bank to pay the bill.

why.en: Use to + infinitive for purpose, never for to.
why.es: «Para pagar» = to pay, no for to pay.

mistakes.wrong: She called a taxi for arriving on time.
mistakes.right: She called a taxi to arrive on time.

why.en: For + -ing describes the use of a thing, not a person's purpose.
why.es: For + -ing sirve para el uso de un objeto; con personas, to + infinitivo.

mistakes.wrong: I'll take a coat in case it will rain.
mistakes.right: I'll take a coat in case it rains.

why.en: After in case use the present simple for the future.
why.es: Después de in case, presente simple, no will.

mistakes.wrong: We'll go out unless it doesn't rain.
mistakes.right: We'll go out unless it rains.

why.en: Unless already means if not, so do not make the verb negative.
why.es: Unless ya es «si no»; no pongas doble negación.

examples.en: He took a second job in order to pay off his loan.
examples.es: Aceptó un segundo trabajo para pagar su préstamo.

examples.en: Write it down so that you don't forget.
examples.es: Apúntalo para que no se te olvide.

examples.en: I always carry a charger in case my phone dies.
You can park here provided that you leave before eight.
We won't get a refund unless we have the receipt.
She spoke quietly so as not to wake the baby.
This app is for tracking your expenses.
I'll lend you the book as long as you return it soon.
Let's book the table now in case the restaurant gets busy.

practice.prompt: I'm learning Italian ___ work in Milan.

explanation.en: The subject is the same, so in order to + infinitive works; for and so that do not fit.

practice.prompt: Take a sandwich ___ you get hungry on the train.

explanation.en: In case describes a precaution against a possible problem.

practice.prompt: You can use my laptop ___ you look after it.

explanation.en: As long as means only if, a condition.

practice.prompt: I'll call you tonight ___ you can tell me the news.

explanation.en: The subjects are different (I / you), so so that + clause fits.
